title: BurstBench: elastic session burst simulator for SSE & WebSocket streaming
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement BurstBench: a production-focused load harness that simulates realistic streaming chat/completions traffic over SSE and WebSocket. Goals: measure tokens/sec under realistic client mixes, track p95/p99 generation latency at tenant and route granularity, and provide automated regression detection for CI and nightly runs. The harness must be KV-cache aware, support prefix caching and repeat request dedup scenarios, emulate connection churn and multiplexed sessions, and generate labeled telemetry suitable for downstream dashboards and statistical detectors.
acceptance_criteria: Can reproduce configurable traffic mixes: short-turn (avg 16 tokens), mid-turn (avg 64 tokens), long-turn (avg 512 tokens) across SSE and WS transports
Produce stable aggregate throughput profiles up to 1,000,000 tokens/sec in a multi-node driver cluster when provisioned with representative hardware
P95 generation latency reported per-route with 95% confidence intervals; p95 regression detector raises alert on >15% sustained increase compared to baseline
Harness emits Prometheus and structured JSON events: connection events, stream-emit latency per token, KV cache hit/miss, backpressure events, and client-side retry counts
Automated CI job that fails on regression detection and uploads time-series and sample payloads to artifact store
Support replay of anonymized production traces and synthetic stochastic user generator (Markov-driven prompt lengths)
Documentation and a runbook for running local/dev cluster and cloud-scale runs, with cost estimate guidance
implementation_notes: Architecture: coordinator + pool of worker drivers. Coordinator schedules scenarios, collects telemetry, normalizes time and injects deterministic seeds for reproducibility
Worker modes: pure-synthetic generator, trace-replayer, and hybrid (trace + noise) to exercise unseen edge cases
KV cache simulation: drivers maintain per-tenant prefix cache model; driver can toggle pre-warm, cold-start, and partial-hit distributions
Telemetry schema: flat JSON lines with fields: timestamp_iso, driver_id, session_id, tenant_id, transport, tokens_generated, token_latency_ms, kv_cache_status, backpressure_ms, response_length_tokens
Regression detection: bootstrap baseline store (time-windowed), use two-phase detector: non-parametric CUSUM + Bayesian change-point to minimize false positives on diurnal noise
CI integration: nightly prober and PR gate that runs short smoke then extended nightly sweep. Artifacts archived to S3 with stable naming: burstbench/{date}/{run-id}
Safety: rate-limit staging credentials, throttle secrets, and fuzz workspace names to avoid accidental writes to prod resources
test_plan: Unit tests for coordinator scheduling and deterministic replay seeding
Integration test: single-node driver against local sandbox runtime with TLS and reverse-proxy to validate SSE and WS paths
Scale tests: k8s job to spin driver fleet across N instances, drive up to targeted tokens/sec and measure end-to-end telemetry
Scenario matrix: combination of transport (SSE/WS), cache state (cold/partial/hot), multiplexing (1:1, 1:N), and token distribution (short/mid/long)
Chaos tests: simulate partial node failure, delayed KV store, and transient region outage to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies
Regression sensitivity validation: inject synthetic regressions (introduce +20% token latency) and assert detector fires within configured window
